findings.title: Malicious match hosts can replay arbitrary guest-memory writes and TU1.5 entrypoints
findings.root_cause: The replay transcript is treated as both evidence of deterministic execution and authorization to perform every recorded operation. Grammar and transcript consistency are therefore substituted for a receiver-owned capability policy.

findings.title: One pinned peer can permanently consume the shared federation listing bank
findings.root_cause: Durable anti-replay high-water marks and active listing capacity share one undifferentiated global table and quota, without origin isolation, local reservation, or bounded reclamation.

findings.title: Steam sign-out destroys its revocation credential before confirming remote revocation
findings.root_cause: The client conflates local forgetting with remote revocation and does not preserve a retryable revocation capability until the server confirms success.

findings.title: Established raw-LAN gameplay datagrams lack cryptographic authentication
findings.root_cause: A cleartext connection cookie is used as a bearer authenticator for established UDP traffic even though any adjacent observer can copy it; no per-session secret is used to authenticate packet contents and sequence.

findings.title: A malicious match host can persist unverified postgame fields for other players
findings.root_cause: Consensus proves that all participants received the same host-supplied bytes, not that each player validated every field later attributed to them.

findings.title: A pinned federation peer can shadow another origin's listing by copying its public server identity
findings.root_cause: The implementation treats a globally derived server identifier as portable across origins but accepts origin-signed listings without a server-key signature, then removes the origin namespace during conflict resolution and client parsing.

findings.title: One malicious survivor can equivocate and split successor-host authority
findings.root_cause: Pairwise transport authentication identifies a sender but does not make that sender's vote globally consistent. The migration protocol applies crash-tolerant majority logic under a threat model that includes malicious admitted peers.

findings.title: Loopback Steam resume can disclose saved refresh credentials to an ambient HTTP proxy
findings.root_cause: URL validation constrains the logical host but does not constrain libcurl's effective network destination; the credential-bearing Steam helper inherits ambient proxy configuration.

findings.title: Discord account linking bypasses the global player-record capacity
findings.root_cause: Player capacity is enforced in one helper rather than at the shared table/allocator boundary, and the linking workflow reimplements creation.

findings.title: One authenticated player can occupy the global serialized EOS verification queue
findings.root_cause: Global queue capacity is accounted before acquiring the serialized worker and without a lock-wait deadline or per-principal concurrency limit.
